ideas.description: Exploit; this combines the E009 near-miss with extra epochs. Start from the E007 Muon incumbent (128/384/576, Muon lr 0.24 / momentum 0.6 / 3 NS steps, batch 2000, ls 0.3, alternating flip, max-autotune, subset whitening). Cut group 1 from 3 convs to 2, exactly as in E009 (same pooling position, width 128). Raise epochs from 9.0 to 9.5 (about 238 steps) and stretch the LR schedule to match. Change nothing else. Warm up the new shapes in build. Log ms/step and per-seed accuracy.
ideas.expected: Per-step time is about 35 ms (E009), so time is about 8.4-8.5 s, versus 8.71 s for the incumbent. Accuracy should be 0.754-0.757: E009's 0.7515 plus 0.5 epoch at a Muon slope of about 0.6-1.0 pp/epoch. If accuracy is >=0.753, this is the new incumbent at about -3% time. If it is 0.750-0.753, go to 9.75 epochs.

ideas.description: Exploit; this is E011's contingency. Progressive resizing on the Muon incumbent, with more total epochs. Use 10.5 epochs in total. Train the first 50% of epochs on whole augmented images downscaled to 24 px on the GPU (bilinear F.interpolate; AdaptiveMaxPool2d(1) as in E011) and the rest at 32 px. Define the LR schedule over total steps. Compile with dynamic=False and warm up both shapes in build, so nothing recompiles in the timed region. Keep everything else at E007.
ideas.expected: From E011 (train 6.79 s at 9 epochs), a full-res epoch costs about 0.96 s and a 24 px epoch about 0.55 s. That puts time near 5.25x0.96 + 5.25x0.55 + 0.06 = about 8.0 s, roughly -8% against 8.71 s. Accuracy should be 0.753-0.758: 0.746 plus 1.5 epochs at about 0.5-0.8 pp/epoch. If it reaches >=0.753 it becomes the new incumbent. If it misses by <0.3 pp, try 11 epochs.

ideas.description: Control to measure the exchange rate. Run the E007 Muon incumbent unchanged except for 8.5 epochs instead of 9.0 (about 213 steps), with the LR schedule stretched to match. This gives the Muon pp/epoch slope that E009, E010, E011 and E013 have to be re-scored against. It also tells us whether trimming epochs on 576 is itself a competitive way to cut time.
ideas.expected: Time about 8.25 s, -0.45 s. Accuracy 0.749-0.752, which implies a slope of 0.5-1.0 pp/epoch. If accuracy holds at >=0.753, the slope is under 0.3 pp/epoch, so epochs are a cheap knob under Muon and this becomes the incumbent. If so, try 8.0 epochs next.

ideas.description: On the E007 Muon incumbent at 9.0 epochs, remove Lookahead and replace the triangular warmup+decay schedule with linear decay from peak to 0, with no warmup, for both the Muon and SGD groups. That is airbench94_muon style. Keep lr, momentum, batch and epochs fixed. Make the change in one run, because both components are SGD-era carryovers.
ideas.expected: Accuracy rises by 0.1-0.4 pp, to about 0.755-0.758. Per-step time falls by about 1% because the Lookahead update goes away. If accuracy is >=+0.2 pp it becomes the new incumbent, and the extra margin can be spent on about 0.25-0.5 fewer epochs. If it falls by >0.2 pp, Lookahead or the warmup is doing work under Muon; next, split them apart.

ideas.description: Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, switch to batch 1536 with Muon lr 0.205 and momentum 0.655 (Hiverge settings). Use the same 9.0 epochs (drop_last, so about 292 steps) and scale the SGD-group lr linearly with batch size. Warm up the new batch shape in build.
ideas.expected: Accuracy +0.1 to +0.3 pp, about 0.755-0.757, from more optimizer steps at the same number of epochs. Time +1 to +3%, about 8.8-8.95 s, from more Newton-Schulz calls and smaller GEMMs. The idea wins only if the gain is >=0.2 pp. In that case trade the gain for -0.25 epoch.

ideas.description: Throughput, numerically near-equivalent. Batch Newton-Schulz across conv weights by grouping same-shape weights into one batched matmul call. Use torch._foreach ops for the SGD updates on biases, BN and the head. Capture the full train step (forward, backward, Muon, SGD) in a CUDA graph with static input buffers, and warm it up in build on synthetic data. Pass the LR schedule as a GPU tensor so per-step LR changes need no recapture. prepare resets all parameter and state tensors in place.
ideas.expected: Train time -3 to -6%, about -0.25 to -0.5 s, removing most of the ~4% Muon overhead and Python launch cost. 3-seed mean accuracy stays within 0.1 pp of 0.7544. If the gain is <1%, launch overhead is not the bottleneck and H2.5 is weakened.

ideas.description: Explore. On the E007 Muon incumbent, add a weight EMA that covers about the last epoch (decay about 0.99 per step at batch 2000, updated only in the final ~25% of steps). Also apply the EMA to the BN running statistics. Evaluate with the EMA weights. Run the EMA update as a single foreach op inside the compiled step. Reset the EMA in prepare.
ideas.expected: 3-seed mean +0.0 to +0.3 pp; per-seed std down >=30%, from about 0.25 to <=0.18 pp; time <=+2%. If the mean rises >=0.2 pp, keep it and spend the margin on fewer epochs. If the mean falls, EMA averages over too-high-LR iterates in this short schedule; drop H4.2.

ideas.description: In build, run 2-3 full optimizer steps on synthetic data: Muon/Newton-Schulz, momentum-buffer allocation, SGD groups, and the backward pass at the training batch shape. Then torch.cuda.synchronize. In prepare, re-init the parameters, buffers and optimizer state in place. Log per-trial train time.
ideas.expected: Trial 1's train time drops by about 0.1-0.15 s, to within 0.05 s of trials 2-3. Mean time falls about 0.05 s (about -0.6%), and accuracy is unchanged (bit-identical if the RNG streams are untouched). It is a small free gain, worth keeping if the drop is >=0.03 s.

structured_output.summary: The queue was empty (all done or dropped), so I added 8 ideas. Exploit: (1) E009's group-1 depth cut plus 0.5 epoch under Muon (H2.4.2, about 8.45 s at about 0.755); (2) progressive resizing, half at 24 px, over 10.5 epochs (H2.3, about 8.0 s at about 0.755). Both build on the best near-misses below 1 pp/s. Next, the missing control for Muon's epoch slope (H1.7.1, 8.5 epochs), which re-scores every pp/s comparison. Then Muon-recipe cleanup (no Lookahead, linear decay; H1.7.2) and batched-NS plus CUDA graph (H2.5.1). Explore: the Hiverge batch-1536 settings (H1.7.3), a late weight EMA for variance and margin (H4.2.1), and warming the optimizer step in build (H3.2.2). Nothing to drop: I010 was already dropped, and no queued idea rests on a settled hypothesis. I left out stacking the depth cut with resizing until each has been measured alone, because both act on the same group-1 layers.
